Color Semantics.content/secondary: Secondary text — labels, section headings, captions, metadata. The lower of the two accessible text levels.
Color Semantics.content/tertiary: NON-ESSENTIAL only — placeholder text, input hints, watermarks. Not captions or metadata: in dark mode this step sits at Lc 27 and cannot be read. Use content-secondary for anything a reader must read.
Color Semantics.content/quaternary: NON-ESSENTIAL only — decorative marks, disabled hints. Never carries information.
Color Semantics.content/inverse: Ink on solid fills — brand buttons, status solids. White in both themes: the solid tone is SOLVED to carry it (see recToneFor).
Color Semantics.background/primary-hover: Hover state for the primary background.
Color Semantics.background/secondary-hover: Hover state for the secondary surface.
Color Semantics.border/brand-alt: Brand border; turns gray in dark mode.
Color Semantics.Surface/page: [ROLE: Base Background] Elevation level 0. Root application background. content.primary and content.secondary must maintain WCAG AA (4.5:1) against this token.
Color Semantics.Surface/layer-1: [ROLE: Container Background] Elevation level 1. Cards, panels, grouped content. Must read slightly distinct from surface.page.
Color Semantics.Surface/layer-2: [ROLE: Elevated Background] Elevation level 2. Popovers, dropdowns, modals. Pair with box-shadow in CSS — the color step alone does not convey floating.
Color Semantics.Surface/input: [ROLE: Form Background] Background for interactive data-entry fields. Ensures content.primary typed by the user stays legible. Same tone as surface.page by design — named separately so forms have their own token.
Color Semantics.Surface/selected: [ROLE: Active State Background] Subtle fill for mutual selection (e.g. a selected table row). Must guarantee 4.5:1 against content.primary on top.
Color Semantics.Surface/inverse: [ROLE: Inverted Background] High-contrast background for tooltips and snackbars. Always pair with content.inverse. Light {neutral.12}; dark {neutral.4} — a muted inverse chip, not the dark ramp's near-white step.
Color Semantics.Surface/overlay: [ROLE: Scrim] Semi-transparent layer over surface.page to focus attention on modals (layer-2 surfaces). Ships at 60% black alpha (`{black-a.8}`), same in both themes.
Color Semantics.Surface/accent: [ROLE: Accent Wash] Ambient brand-tinted background — a section that leans brand without being an interactive fill.
Color Semantics.Content/primary: [ROLE: High Contrast Text] Main body and headings. STRICT: must pass WCAG AA (4.5:1) against surface.page and surface.layer-1.
Color Semantics.Content/secondary: [ROLE: Medium Contrast Text] Supporting copy and descriptions. STRICT: WCAG AA (4.5:1) against standard surface backgrounds.
Color Semantics.Content/subtle: [ROLE: Low Contrast Text] Placeholders and decorative de-emphasis only — not a third readable body tier. Minimum ~3:1; do not convey information.
Color Semantics.Content/disabled: [ROLE: Inactive Text] Disabled controls and copy. Exempt from strict WCAG rules — must communicate inactivity, not full legibility.
Color Semantics.Content/inverse: [ROLE: Inverted Text] Required when the background is surface.inverse or any dark/solid fill outside the accent.
Color Semantics.Content/on-action: [ROLE: Button Text] Label ink used ONLY on action.primary.default. Solved per theme against that fill — never assume white. Must exceed 4.5:1 against the button fill.
Color Semantics.Content/accent: [ROLE: Accent Text] Brand-tinted emphasis — active nav, non-link accent copy. Low-contrast text step (~4.5:1 AA against the page).
Color Semantics.Content/link/default: [ROLE: Interactive Text Default] Actionable link text. Must contrast with the background (4.5:1) and remain distinguishable from adjacent content.primary (~3:1). Uses the ramp text step, not a fill-hover step.
Color Semantics.Content/link/hover: [ROLE: Interactive Text Hover] Hover/focus variation of content.link.default — one ramp step for visible feedback while staying accessible.
Color Semantics.Action/primary/default: [ROLE: Primary CTA Default] Primary call-to-action fill. Inner text must always be content.on-action. Solved per theme — not pinned to a fixed accent step.
Color Semantics.Action/primary/hover: [ROLE: Primary CTA Hover] Interactive hover state. SOLVED one tone past the RESOLVED action.primary.default, re-verified for label contrast — not a fixed accent step. A pinned {accent.10} measured under WCAG AA (as low as 1.78:1) for any hue whose solid resolves above tone 9.
Color Semantics.Action/primary/pressed: [ROLE: Primary CTA Pressed] Active/pressed state. SOLVED two tones past the RESOLVED default, same reasoning as hover. Replaces a fixed dark {accent.6} that measured APCA Lc 0-24 (illegible) once the solid resolves above tone 9, which it does for most hues.
Color Semantics.Action/secondary/default: [ROLE: Secondary CTA Default] Neutral subtle button fill. Label text must be content.primary, not content.on-action.
Color Semantics.Action/secondary/accent: [ROLE: Secondary Accent Fill] Accent-tinted secondary button background. Pair with content.primary for the label.
Color Semantics.Action/disabled: [ROLE: Disabled Action Fill] Disabled button/control background. No contrast floor — communicates inactive state visually.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/neutral/hover: [ROLE: Ghost Neutral Hover] Hover wash for a borderless button with no brand intent (toolbar icons, close buttons, menu items). Flips ink per appearance — {black-a.1} in light, {white-a.1} in dark — because a neutral wash has to darken a light page and lighten a dark one.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/neutral/pressed: [ROLE: Ghost Neutral Pressed] Pressed wash for a neutral borderless button. One step deeper than the hover, same black/white flip.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/brand/hover: [ROLE: Ghost Brand Hover] Hover wash for a borderless button carrying brand intent (tertiary CTA). An ALPHA primitive, not a solid tint — a ghost button has no fill of its own, so its hover has to composite over whatever surface it sits on.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/brand/pressed: [ROLE: Ghost Brand Pressed] Pressed wash for a brand ghost button. One step deeper than action.ghost.brand.hover on the same alpha ramp.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/danger/hover: [ROLE: Ghost Danger Hover] Hover wash for a borderless destructive action (a Delete in a row menu). Error family so the intent reads before the click, not after.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/danger/pressed: [ROLE: Ghost Danger Pressed] Pressed wash for a destructive borderless action.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for error alerts and banners. Pair with status.critical.content — never a fixed ink on the bg alone.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Solid fill for destructive badges and buttons. Pair with status.critical.on-solid. Light solves {error.solid}; dark uses {error.12} so the fill still reads as coloured on a dark page.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Error message ink on status.critical.surface. Both themes {error.11} — chromatic severity, not the near-white {error.12} in dark.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.critical.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for warning alerts. Pair with status.warning.content.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Warning message ink on status.warning.surface. Light and dark both {warning.11} — chromatic severity, not the near-white {warning.12} in dark.
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for success alerts. Pair with status.success.content.
Color Semantics.Status/success/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Success message ink on status.success.surface. Light and dark both {success.11} — chromatic severity, not the near-white {success.12} in dark.
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for informational alerts and banners. Pair with status.info.content — never a fixed ink on the bg alone.
Color Semantics.Status/info/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Info message ink on status.info.surface. Both themes {info.11} — same chromatic-severity rule as critical/warning/success, not the near-white {info.12}.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Solid fill for warning badges and pills. Pair with status.warning.on-solid. Light solves {warning.solid}; dark uses {warning.12} so the fill still reads as coloured on a dark page.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.warning.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill, never assumed white — a warning solid is usually light enough to need dark ink.
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Solid fill for success badges and pills. Pair with status.success.on-solid. Light solves {success.solid}; dark uses {success.12}.
Color Semantics.Status/success/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.success.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill.
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Solid fill for info badges and pills. Pair with status.info.on-solid. Light solves {info.solid}; dark uses {info.12}.
Color Semantics.Status/info/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.info.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] The stroke around a critical alert or banner — the edge of a MESSAGE, not a control boundary, so it is not measured for WCAG 1.4.11 (the severity is carried by status.critical.content and the glyph). An alpha primitive, {error-a.6}, because the tint it sits on is alpha too: a solid stroke over a translucent fill composites against a different backdrop than the fill and the two drift apart on any non-page surface. For a stroke that DOES bear a boundary obligation — an invalid input — use border.critical.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] The stroke around a warning alert or banner. {warning-a.6}. See status.critical.border for why it is alpha and why it carries no contrast floor.
Color Semantics.Status/success/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] The stroke around a success alert or banner. {success-a.6}. See status.critical.border.
Color Semantics.Status/info/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] The stroke around an informational alert or banner. {info-a.6}. See status.critical.border.
Color Semantics.Border/subtle: [ROLE: Decorative Border 1/3] The lightest neutral stroke — hairline dividers, table rules, the edge of a quiet grouping. Light {neutral.3} (ΔL 0.072 from the page), dark {neutral-dark.4}. DECORATION: it separates regions and carries no state, so it has no contrast floor. If the stroke is the only thing telling the user a control is there, that is border.control, not this.
Color Semantics.Border/default: [ROLE: Decorative Border 2/3] The default neutral outline — a card edge, a panel boundary, a grouping box. Light {neutral.4} (ΔL 0.112), dark {neutral-dark.5}. DECORATION, no contrast floor. NOTE: this role changed meaning — it used to BE the control boundary. That job is border.control now; the neutral ramp generates six rungs in this band and the old split used two of them, so a designer reaching for a visible-but-quiet outline had nothing between 0.072 and 0.352.
Color Semantics.Border/strong: [ROLE: Decorative Border 3/3] The heaviest neutral outline that is still decoration — a grouping that needs to read before its neighbours. Light {neutral.5} (ΔL 0.156), dark {neutral-dark.6}. Anything that says "this control is selected / focused / active" conveys state and falls under WCAG 1.4.11: use border.focus or border.control-hover, not this.
Color Semantics.Border/control: [ROLE: Control Boundary] The resting border for inputs, selects, checkboxes, unfilled buttons — anywhere the stroke is the only sign of a control. WCAG 1.4.11 + APCA Lc 45 against the page. SOLVED from tone 8, not pinned there: a fixed tone 8 measured 2.96-2.98:1 on a neutral ramp tinted by certain accents. Light lands on {neutral.8} = 3.26:1/Lc60 for the default seed. Dark starts the same walk at 8 and lands on {neutral-dark.11} = 11.99:1/Lc75 — not tone-for-tone with light; this ramp's dark tones 9-10 pass WCAG but fail APCA (Lc 21-27). Carries the guarantee border.default used to.
Color Semantics.Border/control-hover: [ROLE: Control Boundary Hover] The hover and emphasis step of border.control — one step past whatever that role RESOLVED to ({ui+:...}), never a fixed tone: pinning it to 9 would collapse it onto the boundary on exactly the tinted-neutral systems where the boundary itself walks to 9, leaving no hover state at all. Light {neutral.9} = 4.78:1, dark {neutral-dark.12} = 15.19:1 for the default seed. This is what border.strong used to mean.
Color Semantics.Border/focus: [ROLE: A11y Focus Ring] Keyboard focus-visible ring. SOLVED per theme, not pinned — the ring is always the user's own accent hue, so a fixed tone cannot promise a floor. Light walks the accent ramp from tone 9 until WCAG 1.4.11 + APCA Lc 45 clear (lands on 9-11 depending on hue). Dark stays {accent.11}. Deliberate scope: this is the ONLY focus ring, incl. on an invalid/critical field — focus wins over the error colour rather than a separate border.focus.critical, matching Material/Carbon (WCAG does not require an error-coloured ring) and keeping one ring token instead of one per severity. That scope covers the solid BOUNDARY only — the translucent halo around it is border.ring.*, which does vary by severity.
Color Semantics.Border/ring/default: [ROLE: Focus Halo] Translucent glow outside border.focus. Decoration, NOT a boundary — never measured for WCAG 1.4.11; border.focus is the contrast-bearing part. Replaces a hardcoded 40% alpha in the preview specimens.
Color Semantics.Border/ring/critical: [ROLE: Focus Halo Critical] Focus halo on a field already showing border.critical, so the glow matches the field rather than fighting it. The solid focus boundary stays accent — see border.focus.
Color Semantics.Border/ring/success: [ROLE: Focus Halo Success] Focus halo on a field showing a success/validated border.
Color Semantics.Border/rim-highlight: [ROLE: Elevation Rim] 1px light rim along the top of an elevated surface in dark mode. Below a near-black page only ~5% of the luminance range is left to spend downward, so elevation has to be bought with light, not shadow — this is the token for the rim darkShadow() already paints.
Color Semantics.Border/accent: [ROLE: Decorative Brand Border] Brand-tinted grouping stroke. NOT a state indicator — use border.focus for focus/selected/active.
Color Semantics.Border/critical: [ROLE: Critical Border] Validation stroke for inputs in an error state. Light {error.9} = 3.76:1. Dark {error.11} = 11.94:1 — error.9/10 fail APCA in dark (Lc 37.6/44.2), same blind spot as border.default.
Color Semantics.Border/warning: [ROLE: Warning Border] Validation stroke for inputs in a warning state. {warning.11} — the minimum tone that clears WCAG in light (tone 9 = 2.35, tone 10 = 2.75, both fail).
Color Semantics.Border/success: [ROLE: Success Border] Validation stroke for inputs in a success/valid state. {success.10} — one step lighter than warning/critical; this ramp clears both metrics a full step earlier (3.31:1/Lc60 light, 8.22:1/Lc56 dark).

Radius.role/control: Checkbox, nested child, menu item, inner thumb.

Spacing.role/gap-tight: Icon + label, chip dismiss, inline meta.
Spacing.role/gap-control: Button groups, OTP cells, field + helper.
Spacing.role/inset-page: Page and sheet margins when Grid is unused.

Size.role/hit: Close button and icon-only hit area.

Selector.role/compact: The same glyphs in a dense row or table.
Selector.role/indicator: Badge dot, status pip, unread marker.

Grid.role/desktop: Min-width where desktop type and 12-col grid start.
Grid.role/mobile: Max-width cut: calc(primitive − 1px). Default type and 4-col grid.

Typography.role/heading-xs/size: Overline-scale titles still read as headings.
Typography.role/heading-xs/weight: Overline-scale titles still read as headings.
Typography.role/heading-xs/family: Overline-scale titles still read as headings.
